core_obligations: Reformulate the statement (proof lines 3336-3341): the assertion is that R-Gamma(X, direct sum of E_i) equals the direct sum of R-Gamma(X, E_i) for a family of bounded below objects whose direct sum is again bounded below.

Choose a hypercovering and representatives (proof lines 3341-3351): take a hypercovering K of X whose degree n term is a single affine weakly contractible scheme U_n; pick a common lower bound N below which the cohomology of all E_i vanishes and choose complexes E_i^bullet representing E_i with terms vanishing below N, so that the termwise direct sum represents the direct sum of the E_i.

Compare the total complexes (proof lines 3351-3364): by the hypercovering computation both sides are total complexes of the associated double complexes of sections over K, and because each U_n is quasi-compact the sections of the direct sum over U_n are the direct sum of the sections, so the total complexes agree; hence R-Gamma commutes with direct sums.
Homotopy colimits (proof lines 3364-3367): since R-Gamma is an exact functor of triangulated categories and commutes with direct sums, it commutes with homotopy colimits as a formal consequence.
proof_roadmap: Reduce the statement to a comparison of total complexes over a suitable hypercovering.
Use that sections over quasi-compact objects commute with direct sums to identify the two total complexes.
Derive the statement for homotopy colimits formally.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme X the derived global sections functor on the bounded below derived category of the pro-etale site commutes with direct sums and with homotopy colimits (statement lines 3329-3334). The proof (proof lines 3336-3369) computes both sides through a hypercovering by affine weakly contractible schemes and identifies the total complexes using that sections over quasi-compact objects commute with direct sums, then deduces the homotopy colimit statement formally. H2: one computation with four inputs, written out in full.
